rationale: The position paper reviews olfactory tests and upper-airway disease. Cinnamon is one diagnostic odor stimulus and appears in protocols for identifying odors or oral flavor samples. Sensing cinnamon as a test stimulus is a genuine sensory lead but is separate from eating it to modify Parkinson olfactory impairment. The review supplies no intervention with cooked turkey for that outcome.

The review distinguishes walnut meal, residual or recovered oil, peptides and polyphenols. Its examples include a walnut-oil motor assay in rotenone flies and distinct walnut-meal behavioral or cell studies. A processing passage mentions grape pomace as a separate substrate. Keep the oil, meal, polyphenol and grape preparations distinct. The original studies summarized here do not isolate an anxiety or depression result for culinary walnut oil or a Parkinson anxiety result for grapes.
